controls.name: Straightness
controls.what: How straight a line on a surface is, or the median line of a pin or hole.
controls.summary: Straightness controls single lines. On a surface, each line element must fit between two parallel lines. Put on the size of a pin or hole, the median line must fit inside a cylinder.
controls.mmc: Only on a feature of size
controls.applies: Surface lines, or a pin or hole
controls.check: Indicator along the line, or a CMM
controls.cmp: Straightness never takes a datum and checks lines, not the whole surface.
controls.scan: Each line of the surface must sit between two parallel lines, one tolerance apart. No datum is used.
controls.sketch: A wavy line between two parallel straight lines.

cell.zone: On a surface, each line element must sit between two parallel lines one tolerance apart. On the size of a pin or hole, with a diameter symbol, the median line must sit inside a cylinder of that diameter.
cell.datum: Straightness never takes a datum. Form tolerances compare a feature only with itself.
cell.mmc: Straightness can take M or L only when it is put on the size of a feature, where it controls the median line. Then the tolerance may even be larger than the size tolerance.
cell.applies: Use it on line elements of a flat or round surface, or on the median line of a pin or hole.
cell.also: Straightness holds only the lines it is put on. It does not control flatness of the whole surface.
cell.confused: Shop practice: straightness is often mixed up with flatness. Straightness checks lines one at a time. Flatness checks the whole surface at once.
cell.check: Shop practice: run an indicator along the line, or measure points along it with a CMM.

controls.name: Flatness
controls.what: How flat a surface is, or the median plane of a width.
controls.summary: Flatness controls a whole surface at once. Every point must fit between two parallel planes one tolerance apart. Put on the size of a width, it controls the median plane instead.
controls.mmc: Only on a width feature of size
controls.applies: Surface, or a width feature of size
controls.check: Surface plate and indicator, or a CMM
controls.scan: Every point of the surface must sit between two parallel planes, one tolerance apart. No datum is used.
controls.sketch: A wavy surface inside a slab made of two parallel planes.

cell.zone: The whole surface must sit between two parallel planes one tolerance apart. The planes can tilt freely, because no datum holds them.
cell.datum: Flatness never takes a datum. It compares the surface only with itself.
cell.mmc: Flatness can take M or L only when it is put on the size of a width, such as a tab. Then it controls the median plane.
cell.applies: Use it on a single surface, or on the size of a width feature to control its median plane.
cell.also: Because the whole surface sits in one zone, each straight line on that surface is held to the same width too.
cell.confused: Shop practice: flatness is often mixed up with parallelism. Flatness has no datum. Parallelism holds the surface parallel to a datum.
cell.check: Shop practice: support the part, sweep an indicator over the surface, or measure points with a CMM.

controls.name: Circularity
controls.summary: Circularity checks one circle at a time. Each cross-section of the surface must fit between two concentric circles. Each section is judged on its own.
controls.applies: Round surface: cylinder, cone or sphere
controls.cmp: Circularity never takes a datum and checks one circle at a time.
controls.scan: Each cross-section of the surface must sit between two concentric circles, one tolerance apart. No datum is used.
controls.sketch: An out-of-round circle between two concentric circles.

cell.zone: At each cross-section, the circle of the surface must sit between two concentric circles. Their radii differ by the tolerance.
cell.datum: Circularity never takes a datum. Each circle is judged only against itself.
cell.mmc: Circularity never takes M or L. It is a surface control.
cell.applies: Use it on a round surface, such as a cylinder, a cone or a sphere. Point the frame at the surface, not at the size.
cell.also: Circularity does not hold the sections to each other. A part can be round at every section and still be bent or tapered.
cell.confused: Shop practice: circularity is often mixed up with cylindricity and circular runout. Cylindricity checks the whole cylinder. Circular runout uses a datum axis.
cell.check: Shop practice: use a roundness tester, or measure points around each section with a CMM.

controls.name: Cylindricity
controls.what: How round and straight a whole cylinder is.
controls.summary: Cylindricity checks the whole cylinder at once. The surface must fit between two concentric cylinders. It covers roundness and straightness together.
controls.cmp: Cylindricity never takes a datum and checks the whole cylinder at once.
controls.scan: The whole surface must sit between two concentric cylinders, one tolerance apart. No datum is used.
controls.sketch: A wavy cylinder surface between two concentric cylinders, seen from the side.

cell.zone: The whole surface must sit between two concentric cylinders. Their radii differ by the tolerance.
cell.datum: Cylindricity never takes a datum. The two cylinders can sit anywhere that fits the surface.
cell.mmc: Cylindricity never takes M or L. It is a surface control.
cell.applies: Use it on a cylindrical surface. Point the frame at the surface, not at the size.
cell.also: Cylindricity includes circularity, straightness and taper of the cylinder in one control.
cell.confused: Shop practice: cylindricity is often mixed up with total runout. Total runout uses a datum axis. Cylindricity does not.
cell.check: Shop practice: measure many points over the surface with a CMM or a cylindricity tester.

controls.name: Perpendicularity
controls.what: A surface, axis or centre plane held at 90° to a datum.
controls.summary: Perpendicularity holds a feature at 90 degrees to a datum. A surface or centre plane must fit between two parallel planes. An axis can use a cylinder instead.
controls.zone: 2 planes, or a cylinder for an axis
controls.mmc: Yes, on a feature of size
controls.check: Angle plate and indicator, or a CMM
controls.cmp: Perpendicularity always takes a datum and holds 90 degrees to it.
controls.scan: The surface must sit between two parallel planes at 90 degrees to the datum, one tolerance apart.
controls.sketch: A datum line labelled A, with two parallel lines standing at 90 degrees to it and a wavy surface between them.

cell.zone: A surface or centre plane must sit between two parallel planes at 90 degrees to the datum. With a diameter symbol, an axis must sit inside a cylinder at 90 degrees to the datum.
cell.datum: Perpendicularity always needs a datum. The 90 degrees is measured from it.
cell.mmc: Perpendicularity can take M or L when it is put on a feature of size, such as a hole or pin. On a plain surface it cannot.
cell.applies: Use it on a flat surface, or on the axis or centre plane of a feature of size.
cell.also: On a flat surface it also controls flatness, up to the same tolerance, unless the tangent plane symbol is used. It does not locate the surface.
cell.confused: Shop practice: perpendicularity is often mixed up with position. Perpendicularity only holds the angle. Position also locates the feature.
cell.check: Shop practice: set the part on its datum, use an angle plate or square and sweep an indicator, or use a CMM.

controls.name: Parallelism
controls.what: A surface, axis or centre plane held parallel to a datum.
controls.summary: Parallelism holds a feature parallel to a datum. A surface or centre plane must fit between two planes parallel to the datum. An axis can use a cylinder instead.
controls.zone: 2 planes, or a cylinder for an axis
controls.mmc: Yes, on a feature of size
controls.check: Part on the datum, indicator across the surface
controls.cmp: Parallelism always takes a datum and holds the feature parallel to it.
controls.scan: The surface must sit between two planes parallel to the datum, one tolerance apart.
controls.sketch: A datum line labelled A, with two parallel lines above it and a wavy surface between them.

cell.zone: A surface or centre plane must sit between two planes parallel to the datum. With a diameter symbol, an axis must sit inside a cylinder parallel to the datum.
cell.datum: Parallelism always needs a datum. The surface is held parallel to it.
cell.mmc: Parallelism can take M or L when it is put on a feature of size. On a plain surface it cannot.
cell.applies: Use it on a flat surface, or on the axis or centre plane of a feature of size.
cell.also: On a flat surface it also controls flatness, up to the same tolerance, unless the tangent plane symbol is used. It does not set the distance from the datum.
cell.confused: Shop practice: parallelism is often mixed up with flatness. Flatness has no datum. Parallelism always has one.
cell.check: Shop practice: rest the part on its datum face and sweep an indicator across the surface.

controls.name: Angularity
controls.what: A surface, axis or centre plane held at a basic angle to a datum.
controls.summary: Angularity holds a feature at a basic angle to a datum. A surface or centre plane must fit between two parallel planes at that angle. An axis can use a cylinder instead.
controls.zone: 2 planes, or a cylinder for an axis
controls.mmc: Yes, on a feature of size
controls.check: Sine bar and indicator, or a CMM
controls.cmp: Angularity always takes a datum and holds a basic angle to it.
controls.scan: The surface must sit between two parallel planes at the basic angle to the datum, one tolerance apart.
controls.sketch: A datum line labelled A, with two parallel lines inclined to it and a wavy surface between them.

cell.zone: A surface or centre plane must sit between two parallel planes at the basic angle to the datum. With a diameter symbol, an axis must sit inside a cylinder at that angle.
cell.datum: Angularity always needs a datum. The basic angle is measured from it.
cell.mmc: Angularity can take M or L when it is put on a feature of size. On a plain surface it cannot.
cell.applies: Use it on a flat surface, or on the axis or centre plane of a feature of size. The angle itself is a basic dimension.
cell.also: On a flat surface it also controls flatness, up to the same tolerance, unless the tangent plane symbol is used.
cell.confused: Shop practice: angularity is often mixed up with an angle that has a plus or minus tolerance. That kind of angle gives a zone that widens away from the corner. Angularity gives two parallel planes.
cell.check: Shop practice: tilt the part to the angle on a sine bar and sweep an indicator, or use a CMM.

controls.name: Position
controls.what: Where the axis, centre plane or centre point of a feature of size sits.
controls.summary: Position locates a feature of size from its true position. Its axis or centre plane must sit inside the zone. With M, the surface must also stay clear of a fixed boundary.
controls.also: Orientation of the axis or centre plane
controls.check: CMM, or a functional gauge at MMC
controls.cmp: Position locates a feature of size, usually from datums.
controls.orient: Yes, of the axis or centre plane
controls.scan: The axis of the hole must sit inside a cylinder centred on its true position. The datums set where true position is.
controls.sketch: A cross marking true position, a circle for the cylindrical zone around it, and a dot for the actual axis inside the zone.

cell.zone: With a diameter symbol, the zone is a cylinder centred on the true position. Without it, the tolerance is the full width between two parallel planes.
cell.datum: Position usually takes datums, which set the true position. It can go without them when the toleranced features set the primary datum, or for coaxial features toleranced to each other.
cell.mmc: Position can take M or L. With M, the zone grows as the feature moves away from its maximum material size. That growth is the bonus tolerance.
cell.applies: Position works only on a feature of size, such as a hole, pin, slot or tab. For a plain surface, use profile.
cell.also: The same zone also limits how far the axis or centre plane can tilt.
cell.confused: Shop practice: position is often mixed up with profile of a surface. Position is for features of size. Profile is for surfaces.
cell.check: Shop practice: measure the feature with a CMM, or use a functional gauge made at the virtual condition when M is used.

controls.name: Profile of a line
controls.what: The shape of a surface, one cross-section at a time.
controls.summary: Profile of a line checks the shape of each line element on its own. Each section must fit between two lines that follow the true profile. Datums are optional.
controls.zone: 2 lines that follow the true profile, per section
controls.also: With datums: orientation and location of each line
controls.check: CMM scan, or an optical comparator
controls.cmp: Profile of a line can go either way, and with datums it also orients and locates each line.
controls.scan: Each section of the surface must sit between two lines that follow the true profile. The zone is one tolerance wide.
controls.sketch: A curved line between two curves that follow the true profile.

cell.zone: At each section, the line of the surface must sit between two lines that follow the true profile. They sit equally either side of it unless the U symbol says otherwise.
cell.datum: Profile of a line can be used with or without datums. Without datums it controls shape only.
cell.mmc: Profile never takes M or L on the tolerance. M or L may appear only on its datum references.
cell.applies: Use it when each line element of a surface matters, but the surface as a whole does not need one zone.
cell.also: With datums, it can also hold the orientation and location of each line.
cell.confused: Shop practice: it is often mixed up with profile of a surface. Profile of a line checks one section at a time. Profile of a surface checks the whole surface at once.
cell.check: Shop practice: scan sections with a CMM, or compare the outline on an optical comparator.

controls.name: Profile of a surface
controls.what: The shape of a whole surface, or of several surfaces.
controls.summary: Profile of a surface checks a whole surface at once. The surface must fit between two boundaries that follow the true profile. With datums it also orients and locates the surface.
controls.zone: 2 surfaces that follow the true profile
controls.also: Form; with datums, orientation and location too
controls.check: CMM against the model, or a 3D scan
controls.cmp: Profile of a surface can go either way, and with datums it also orients and locates the surface.
controls.scan: The whole surface must sit between two boundaries that follow the true profile. The zone is one tolerance wide.
controls.sketch: A curved surface between two boundaries that follow the true profile, drawn with depth.

cell.zone: The whole surface must sit between two boundaries that follow the true profile. They sit equally either side of it unless the U symbol says otherwise.
cell.datum: Profile of a surface can be used with or without datums. Each datum it references adds orientation or location control.
cell.mmc: Profile never takes M or L on the tolerance. M or L may appear only on its datum references.
cell.applies: Use it on a surface of any shape, flat or curved, or on several surfaces together.
cell.also: It always controls form. With datums it also controls orientation and location. On its own, the zone also limits size where the surfaces form a size.
cell.confused: Shop practice: it is often mixed up with position. Profile is for surfaces. Position is for features of size.
cell.check: Shop practice: measure the surface with a CMM against the model, or compare a 3D scan.

controls.name: Circular runout
controls.what: Each circle of a surface, held to a datum axis.
controls.summary: Circular runout checks each circle of the surface on its own, relative to a datum axis. Each circle must fit between two circles centred on that axis. On a face, it limits wobble.
controls.zone: 2 circles on the datum axis, per section
controls.applies: Surfaces round a datum axis, or faces at 90° to it
controls.also: Form and coaxiality of each circle; on a face, wobble
controls.check: Part turned on its datum, indicator held still
controls.cmp: Circular runout always takes a datum axis and checks one circle at a time.
controls.scan: Each circle of the surface must sit between two circles centred on the datum axis, one tolerance apart.
controls.sketch: End view: a centre mark for datum axis A, two circles centred on it, and the part circle between them.

cell.zone: At each section, the circle of the surface must sit between two circles centred on the datum axis, one tolerance apart. On a face, each circle must sit between two circles of the same size, one tolerance apart along the axis.
cell.datum: Circular runout always needs a datum axis. The datum is applied regardless of material boundary.
cell.mmc: Runout never takes M or L, and its datum is used regardless of material boundary.
cell.applies: Use it on surfaces built around a datum axis, such as cylinders and cones, or on faces at 90 degrees to that axis.
cell.also: Around the axis it limits the combined form and coaxiality of each circle. On a face it limits wobble.
cell.confused: Shop practice: it is often mixed up with total runout and circularity. Total runout covers the whole surface at once. Circularity has no datum.
cell.check: Shop practice: turn the part on its datum and read an indicator held still at each section.

controls.name: Total runout
controls.what: A whole surface, held to a datum axis.
controls.summary: Total runout checks the whole surface at once, relative to a datum axis. A cylinder must fit between two cylinders on that axis. A face must fit between two planes at 90 degrees to it.
controls.zone: 2 cylinders on the datum axis, or 2 planes for a face
controls.applies: Surfaces round a datum axis, or faces at 90° to it
controls.also: Circularity, cylindricity, straightness, coaxiality; on a face, flatness and perpendicularity
controls.check: Part turned on its datum, indicator moved along without reset
controls.cmp: Total runout always takes a datum axis and checks the whole surface at once.
controls.scan: The whole surface must sit between two cylinders centred on the datum axis, one tolerance apart.
controls.sketch: Side view: datum axis A as a centre line, two bands for the two cylinders, the part surface between them, and an arrow along the full length.

cell.zone: Round the axis, the whole surface must sit between two cylinders centred on the datum axis, one tolerance apart. On a face, it must sit between two parallel planes at 90 degrees to the axis.
cell.datum: Total runout always needs a datum axis. The datum is applied regardless of material boundary.
cell.mmc: Runout never takes M or L, and its datum is used regardless of material boundary.
cell.applies: Use it on surfaces built around a datum axis, or on faces at 90 degrees to that axis.
cell.also: Round the axis it limits circularity, cylindricity, straightness and coaxiality together. On a face it limits flatness and perpendicularity.
cell.confused: Shop practice: it is often mixed up with cylindricity. Total runout is held to a datum axis. Cylindricity has no datum.
cell.check: Shop practice: turn the part on its datum and move the indicator along the whole surface without resetting it.

controls.name: Concentricity
controls.what: In 2009: the median points of a surface of revolution, held to a datum axis.
controls.summary: Concentricity was a 2009 control. The median points of a turned surface had to sit inside a cylinder centred on the datum axis. It was removed in 2018. Use position, runout or profile instead.
controls.zone: A cylinder on the datum axis
controls.cmp: Concentricity was a 2009 control, removed in the 2018 edition.
controls.locate: Median points to the datum axis
controls.sketch: End view: datum axis A with a small circular zone around it and median points inside the zone.

cell.zone: In 2009, the median points of all opposed elements had to sit inside a cylinder centred on the datum axis.
cell.datum: In 2009, concentricity always referenced a datum axis, and that datum applied regardless of material boundary.
cell.mmc: In 2009, concentricity applied regardless of feature size only. It could not take M or L.
cell.applies: In 2009 it was used on a surface of revolution. In 2018, use position, runout or profile of a surface for coaxial features.

controls.name: Symmetry
controls.what: In 2009: the median points of opposed surfaces, held to a datum.
controls.summary: Symmetry was a 2009 control. The median points of opposed surfaces had to sit between two parallel planes centred on a datum. It was removed in 2018. Use position or profile instead.
controls.datum: Always, a datum axis or centre plane
controls.cmp: Symmetry was a 2009 control, removed in the 2018 edition.
controls.sketch: A datum centre plane with two parallel planes around it, median points between them, and the two opposed surfaces.

cell.zone: In 2009, the median points of opposed elements had to sit between two parallel planes, centred on the datum.
cell.datum: In 2009, symmetry always referenced a datum axis or centre plane, and that datum applied regardless of material boundary.
cell.mmc: In 2009, symmetry applied regardless of feature size only. It could not take M or L.
cell.applies: In 2009 it was used on opposed surfaces. In 2018, use position or profile for symmetrical features.

modifiers.name: Maximum material condition
modifiers.text: Smallest hole, largest pin. Allows bonus tolerance as the feature moves away from it.

modifiers.name: Least material condition
modifiers.text: Largest hole, smallest pin. Often used to protect a minimum wall.

modifiers.name: Projected tolerance zone
modifiers.text: Moves the zone out of the hole, over the height of the mating part or fastener. Used for threaded and press-fit holes.

modifiers.name: Free state
modifiers.text: This tolerance applies with the part free, on a drawing where other tolerances apply restrained.

modifiers.name: Tangent plane
modifiers.text: Controls only the plane resting on the high points. The form of the surface is not controlled by that tolerance.

modifiers.name: Unequally disposed profile
modifiers.text: Splits a profile zone unequally. The value after U is the part of the zone on the side that adds material.

modifiers.name: Diameter
modifiers.text: Before a tolerance, the zone is a cylinder of that diameter. Before a size, the size is a diameter.

modifiers.name: Basic dimension
modifiers.text: A theoretically exact value in a box. Its tolerance comes from a feature control frame or a note.

modifiers.name: Datum feature
modifiers.text: A letter in a box with a triangle on the real feature. Datums are taken from that feature.

modifiers.name: All around
modifiers.text: A circle on the leader. The tolerance applies all around the outline in that view.

rules.title: Rule #1: size limits form
rules.text: Unless the drawing says otherwise, a regular feature of size may not break a boundary of perfect form at MMC. As it moves toward LMC, its form may vary by the same amount.

rules.title: Rule #2: no modifier means RFS
rules.text: With no M or L after a tolerance, it applies regardless of feature size. With no M or L after a datum letter, the datum applies regardless of material boundary.

rules.title: Bonus tolerance
rules.text: With M, the tolerance grows by how far the feature has moved from its MMC size. Hole Ø9.06 with MMC Ø8.9: bonus 0.16.

rules.title: Virtual condition
rules.text: The fixed boundary made by the MMC size and the tolerance at MMC. Hole at MMC: Ø8.9 − 0.2 = Ø8.7.

rules.title: Position from two offsets
rules.text: For a cylindrical zone, actual position = 2 × √(X² + Y²). With X 0.11 and Y 0.07 it is Ø0.26.

headline.removed: Concentricity and symmetry were removed in Y14.5-2018.
headline.rows2009: The 12 rows follow Y14.5-2018. The two 2009-only rows follow Y14.5-2009.
headline.note2009: This view follows Y14.5-2009. Where 2009 words a rule differently, the 2009 wording is shown. Concentricity and symmetry were removed in Y14.5-2018.

ask.answer: Orientation and runout always need a datum. Position usually does. Profile can go either way. The four form controls never take one.
Six can, when they are put on a feature of size. The other six never take M or L on the tolerance.
The two 2009-only controls never took M or L either. They applied regardless of feature size.
The two 2009-only controls always referenced a datum.

Six can control the axis, centre plane or median line of a feature of size. Position works only on features of size. The other six control surface elements, even when the surface belongs to a feature of size.

Seven cover a whole surface at once: flatness, cylindricity, the three orientation controls on a surface, profile of a surface and total runout. Four work one line or one circle at a time. Position controls an axis or centre plane.

parts.zoneDia: The diameter symbol makes the zone a cylinder. The number is its diameter.
parts.zoneWidth: With no diameter symbol, the number is the full width of the zone.
parts.zoneWidthPos: With no diameter symbol, position uses two parallel planes. The number is the full width between them.
parts.zoneRadial: The number is the distance between the two boundaries of the zone.
parts.zoneProfile: The number is the full width of the profile zone, split equally about the true profile unless U is used.
parts.modNone: No modifier: the tolerance applies regardless of feature size.
parts.modNoneSurface: No modifier is used on a plain surface. Size modifiers belong to features of size only.
parts.modM: M: the stated tolerance applies when the feature is at its maximum material size. As it moves away from that size, the tolerance grows by the same amount.
parts.modL: L: the stated tolerance applies when the feature is at its least material size. As it moves away from that size, the tolerance grows by the same amount.
parts.modP: P: the zone is projected out of the hole, over the height given after the symbol.
parts.modT: T: only a plane resting on the high points of the surface must sit in the zone. Some points of the surface may lie outside it.
parts.modU: U: the zone is split unequally. The second number is how much of the zone is on the side that adds material.
parts.datumNone: No datum: the zone is not held to anything else on the part.
parts.datum1: is the primary datum. It is used first.
parts.datum2: is the secondary datum. It is used after the primary.
parts.datum3: is the tertiary datum. It is used last.
parts.datumMod: M or L after a datum letter means the datum feature applies at its maximum or least material boundary.
parts.orderText: Datum letters are read left to right in order of precedence. They need not be in alphabetical order.

wrong.title: Form controls never take a datum.
wrong.text: Straightness, flatness, circularity and cylindricity compare a feature only with itself, so there is nothing for a datum to hold. Remove the datum, or use an orientation or profile control if the feature must relate to the datum.

wrong.title: Orientation always needs a datum.
wrong.text: Perpendicularity, parallelism and angularity hold a feature at an angle to a datum, so at least one datum must be in the frame.

wrong.title: Runout always needs a datum axis.
wrong.text: Circular and total runout are measured about a datum axis. Add the datum feature that sets that axis.

wrong.title: Runout datums take no M or L.
wrong.text: Runout is held to the datum axis regardless of material boundary, so M or L cannot follow its datum letters.

wrong.title: This control cannot take M or L.
wrong.text: Circularity, cylindricity, profile, runout and orientation on a surface never take M or L on the tolerance. Remove the modifier.

wrong.title: M and L need a feature of size.
wrong.text: M and L apply to tolerances on features of size, such as a hole, pin, slot or tab. A plain surface has no size to depart from.

wrong.title: Position needs a feature of size.
wrong.text: Position locates the axis, centre plane or centre point of a feature of size. To locate a plain surface, use profile of a surface with datums.

wrong.title: A diameter zone needs a cylindrical feature.
wrong.text: The diameter symbol is used only when the zone is a cylinder or sphere, such as for the axis of a hole or pin. Remove it here.

wrong.title: This control has no diameter zone.
wrong.text: Flatness, circularity, cylindricity, profile and runout zones are widths between two boundaries, never a cylinder. Remove the diameter symbol.

wrong.title: This control needs a round surface.
wrong.text: Circularity and cylindricity are defined for surfaces of revolution. They cannot be used on a flat face, a slot or a tab.

wrong.title: Runout needs a surface around the datum axis, or a face at 90° to it.
wrong.text: Runout controls surfaces built around a datum axis and faces at right angles to it. A slot or tab width is not such a surface.

wrong.title: Point this frame at the surface, not at the size.
wrong.text: A circularity or cylindricity callout is put on the surface, not on the size dimension.

wrong.title: Flatness on a size needs a width feature.
wrong.text: Put on a size dimension, flatness controls the median plane of a width, such as a slot or tab. A hole or pin has a median line, not a median plane.

wrong.title: Form here has to be smaller than the size tolerance.
wrong.text: When a form tolerance is put on the surface of a feature of size, it must be smaller than the size tolerance, unless free state or independency applies.

wrong.title: I, O and Q are not used as datum letters.
wrong.text: Datum feature letters may be any letter except I, O and Q.

wrong.title: Each datum letter can appear once.
wrong.text: Each compartment holds a different datum feature, in order of precedence. Repeating a letter does not add a datum.

wrong.title: P is used with position or orientation only.
wrong.text: A projected tolerance zone is specified for a positional or an orientation tolerance. Remove P here.

wrong.title: P needs a hole.
wrong.text: A projected zone is used for threaded or press-fit holes, where a fixed fastener could otherwise lean into the mating part.

wrong.title: U is used with profile only.
wrong.text: The unequally disposed symbol goes in a profile frame, after the tolerance. Remove U here, or use profile.

wrong.title: The U value cannot be larger than the tolerance.
wrong.text: The number after U is the part of the zone that adds material. It must be between zero and the total tolerance.

wrong.title: T is for orientation, and for runout or profile on a flat face.
wrong.text: The tangent plane symbol is shown with orientation tolerances, and may also be used with runout or profile on a planar feature. Remove T here.

wrong.title: T needs a flat face.
wrong.text: A tangent plane rests on the high points of a surface, so T belongs on a flat face, not on a hole, pin or round surface.

wrong.title: Concentricity and symmetry always need a datum.
wrong.text: In 2009, concentricity held median points to a datum axis, and symmetry to a datum axis or centre plane. Add the datum.

wrong.title: Concentricity and symmetry take no M or L.
wrong.text: In 2009, the tolerance applied regardless of feature size only, and the datum regardless of material boundary only. Remove every M and L.

wrong.title: Concentricity needs a surface of revolution.
wrong.text: In 2009, concentricity was for a surface of revolution, such as a hole or pin, with a cylindrical zone. Use a hole or pin and the diameter symbol.

wrong.title: Symmetry needs opposed surfaces.
wrong.text: In 2009, symmetry was for opposed surfaces, such as a slot or tab, with a zone of two parallel planes. Use a slot or tab, without the diameter symbol.

wrong.title: This symbol was removed in Y14.5-2018.
wrong.text: Concentricity and symmetry are no longer in Y14.5-2018. Use position, runout or profile instead.

notes.noDatumPosition: Position with no datum only relates the toleranced features to each other.
notes.axisMethod: This check uses the axis method. With M or L, the standard gives the surface method precedence, and the two can differ when the feature has form error.
notes.lmcSize: With L, the bonus is measured from the least material size, using the actual minimum material envelope.
notes.datumModNote: Datum modifiers are not checked against the datum feature type here.
notes.freeNotOffered: Free state is not offered in the builder, because it needs a restraint note on the drawing.
notes.surfaceOnSize2009: Y14.5-2018 says a circularity or cylindricity callout goes on the surface, not on the size. Y14.5-2009 has no matching statement.

calc.sizeLimits: The measured size must be within the size limits, or the feature is out.
calc.actualPosDia: Actual position for a cylindrical zone = 2 × √(X² + Y²).
calc.actualPosWidth: Actual position for a width zone = 2 × the offset of the centre plane.
calc.bonusMMCHole: Bonus with M, hole = measured size − MMC size (the smallest limit).
calc.bonusMMCPin: Bonus with M, pin = MMC size (the largest limit) − measured size.
calc.bonusLMCHole: Bonus with L, hole = LMC size (the largest limit) − measured size.
calc.bonusLMCPin: Bonus with L, pin = measured size − LMC size (the smallest limit).
calc.bonusRFS: With no modifier the bonus is zero.
calc.verdict: IN when the size is within limits and the actual value is not more than the allowed value.
calc.vcHoleMMC: Virtual condition, hole at M = MMC size − tolerance.
calc.vcPinMMC: Virtual condition, pin at M = MMC size + tolerance.
calc.vcHoleLMC: Virtual condition, hole at L = LMC size + tolerance.
calc.vcPinLMC: Virtual condition, pin at L = LMC size − tolerance.
calc.surfaceValue: For a surface control, the actual value is the width of zone the measured surface needs. It must not be more than the tolerance.
calc.profileSplit: With U, the zone extends by the U value on the side that adds material and by the rest on the side that removes material.
calc.profileEqual: Without U, the profile zone is split equally: half the tolerance each side of the true profile.
calc.gauge: Shop practice: a functional gauge pin for a hole at M is made at the virtual condition size.
calc.notInspection: A learning check, not an inspection record.

patch: Straightness can take M or L only when it is put on the size of a feature, where it controls the median line. Then its value can exceed the size tolerance, except when it is used together with an orientation or position tolerance.
Use it on a round surface, such as a cylinder, a cone or a sphere.
Use it on a cylindrical surface.

At each section, the line of the surface must sit between two lines that follow the true profile. They sit equally either side of it unless the U symbol, or phantom lines on a 2D drawing, show otherwise.
The whole surface must sit between two boundaries that follow the true profile. They sit equally either side of it unless the U symbol, or phantom lines on a 2D drawing, show otherwise.
The number is the full width of the profile zone, split equally about the true profile unless U is used. On a 2D drawing, 2009 also lets phantom lines show an unequal zone.
Without U, and with no phantom lines on the drawing, the profile zone is split equally: half the tolerance each side of the true profile.

Circular runout checks each circle of the surface on its own, relative to a datum axis. As the part turns on that axis, the indicator reading at each circle must not move more than the tolerance. On a face, it limits wobble.
FIM at each circle, on the datum axis

Turn the part on the datum axis. At each circle of the surface, the full indicator movement must not be more than the tolerance. The indicator is held normal to the surface, so on a face it reads along the axis.
Turn the part on the datum axis. At each circle of the surface, the full indicator movement must not be more than the tolerance.

Total runout checks the whole surface at once, relative to a datum axis. As the part turns, the indicator moves along the whole surface, and its full movement must not be more than the tolerance. It works on surfaces round the axis and on faces at 90 degrees to it.
FIM over the whole surface, on the datum axis

Turn the part on the datum axis and move the indicator along the whole surface. The full indicator movement must not be more than the tolerance, on a surface round the axis or on a face at 90 degrees to it.
Turn the part on the datum axis and move the indicator along the whole surface. The full indicator movement must not be more than the tolerance.
Circularity, straightness, coaxiality, angularity, taper; on a face, flatness and perpendicularity
Round the axis it limits circularity, straightness, coaxiality, angularity and taper, and also the profile of the surface. On a face it limits perpendicularity and flatness.
The number is the distance between the two boundaries of the zone. For runout, 2009 states it as the most the indicator may move: the full indicator movement.
Flatness, circularity, cylindricity and profile zones are widths between two boundaries, and runout is read as indicator movement. None of them is a cylinder. Remove the diameter symbol.
Controls only the plane resting on the high points. The flatness of the surface is not controlled by that tolerance.
T: the tolerance applies to the plane that touches the high points of the surface. The flatness of the surface is not controlled by this tolerance.
T is for orientation, or for another control held to a datum.
The tangent plane symbol is shown with orientation tolerances, and may also be used with other controls when the feature is held to a datum. Remove T here.
Free state is not offered in the builder. It is used on drawings with restraint notes, to mark a requirement that applies with the part free.
